evidence.result: BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 10s, 7 actionable tasks: 7 executed. The four new RunReportTest cases pass: 'the split residue is not reported as a fraction of a room', 'the residue this removes is the one the point split actually produces', 'the residue drifts in both directions, which is what the clamp alone missed', 'a negative never reaches the report', plus 'a genuinely unattributed room still counts'.

evidence.result: BASELINE: PASSING. Regression check over the whole suite: build/test-results/test/*.xml sums to classes 11, tests 84, skipped 0, failures 0, errors 0 — up from 79, with no existing test changed or removed.

evidence.result: BUILD SUCCESSFUL. Deliberately not './gradlew build': build is finalizedBy copyToDist, and refreshing dist/sighteaddons-0.9.0.jar would leave the committed jar no longer the released 0.9.0 artifact. 'git status --short dist/' is empty.

features.notes:
NOT a schema change and NOT paired with the receiver: `unattributed` is already in RUN_KEYS (ingest.py:138) and validated as _real(x, 0, MAX_CLEARED) (ingest.py:226), so nothing has to be deployed first and no field is added, removed or retyped. Diff done before touching RunReport.kt, as CLAUDE.md requires. Origin: POINTS_PER_ROOM is 1.0 and DungeonGrid.splitPoints divides it by tick counts, so a room shared three ways credits 0.333... three times and the sum drifts a few ULPs across a floor; roomsCleared - pointsByPlayer().values.sum() then yields a residue instead of a zero. The existing coerceAtLeast(0.0) in RunReport.build was written for exactly this and was one-sided, so +3.55e-15 went through and reached profiles/, which is append-only and can never be corrected. Fixed by ContributionTracker.settle (round to the two decimals every display path already truncates to, then clamp), applied in build() — the documented pure seam, so `write` and any caller passing `unattributed` directly are both covered. RoomHistory.printSummary computed the same expression inline behind its own `> 0.01`; both sites now call ContributionTracker.unattributed(), so the duplicated expression is gone rather than doubled. Genuinely non-zero values are untouched on purpose: a room cleared with nobody ever seen in it is a real unattributed point, and the gap to roomsCleared is the receiver's own diagnostic for a broken decoration mapping (agent/AGENT-PROMPT.md:62). mod_version stays 0.9.0, so the release gate did not fire — which also means the fix reaches players only at the next bump and release.

OPEN REVIEW FINDING, carried here in session 006 so it stops dying in evaluator-rubric.md, which is overwritten wholesale every pass (two reviewers had already hand-copied it forward). Non-blocking, optional, no status change: ContributionTracker.settle's KDoc argues rounding against the OLD CLAMP — 'the clamp this replaces only ever caught the negative half' (ContributionTracker.kt:448) — when the real alternative on the table was a symmetric threshold-to-zero, which would also have caught both signs. The argument as written defeats a weaker option than the one a reader would propose. The behaviour is right and tested; only the justification is aimed at the wrong target. Fix is one paragraph in that KDoc, next time somebody is in this file.

features.notes:
PAIRED with the receiver's schema-001, which was DEPLOYED FIRST and is live on master at f1085a7 — verified before this feature started, so the order CLAUDE.md fixes was respected. CORRECTION TO THIS NOTE'S EARLIER RATIONALE, checked against the receiver's source rather than trusted: this pair has no 400 in it and never did. ingest.py:214 validates `v` as _num(x, 1, 10), so v=5 was already accepted before the receiver moved, and ingest.py:159 has had `enterTick` in ROOM_OPTIONAL since schema 3. No field is added, removed or retyped here — only the meaning of an existing one changes — so nothing would have rejected this build and the 'loses every run of it' claim did not apply. The receiver corrected the mirror image of the same false rationale on its own side. WHAT THE REAL RISK IS, and it is worse than a 400 because it is silent: roomstats.py routes the clear span on the report's `v` alone (STAY_ANCHOR_SCHEMA = 5), below 5 into `clear` and at-or-above into `clearStay`, never mixing them. Shipping the stay anchor with SCHEMA left at 4 would fold every stay-anchored span back into the old sighting-anchored average — no 400, no log line, and profiles/ is append-only so the mean could never be cleaned. Hence SCHEMA 4 -> 5 in RunReport.kt as part of this feature, and a test that fails if the anchor is stay-based while v < 5. WHY IT MATTERS: the receiver's roomstats.py docstring — `clear` was an upper bound, not a duration, because enterTick was stamped the first time ANY party member was seen in the room with no minimum stay, so 145 s got reported for a 1x1. HOW IT IS ANCHORED NOW: TrackedRoom tracks a current stay per member (start, ticks, lastSeen) instead of only the run-long tick total, and enteredAtTick is the start of the first stay to reach MIN_TICKS — its own start, not the tick it qualified at, since the latter would shorten every clear in the data by a flat second. Sighting gaps of up to MIN_TICKS do not split a stay, because PartyTracker.positions deliberately reports no teammate positions at all for the 10-20 ticks around a death. A room that clears before anyone qualifies falls back to the earliest stay begun within the last MIN_TICKS: without that, the empty 1x1s that clear on entry (three in one M7, per the count in ContributionTracker.award) would carry no anchor at all and the server's mean would be built from every room EXCEPT the fastest — a bias rather than sparsity. The fallback's window is what makes it safe, since every span it can produce is under a second by construction and it can never reach back to an old walk-through. Nothing anchors after the clear, so enterTick <= clearTick holds whenever both are set, and a preCleared room now reports a null anchor for its whole life (honest: there is no clear of ours to time, and roomstats.py:102 skips preCleared rooms anyway). enteredAtTick is `private set` so the invariant has exactly one home. NOT SHIPPED: no version bump and no dist/ refresh, so this reaches no install until the next release, which is the user's decision.

THREE OPEN REVIEW FINDINGS, carried here in session 006 so they stop dying in evaluator-rubric.md, which is overwritten wholesale every pass — two reviewers had already hand-copied them forward by hand, and the one finding that was fixed in one file and left live in another (init.sh vs claude-progress.md) is what that costs. All three are non-blocking, none changes this feature's status, and none is a defect in the shipped behaviour.

(1) stay.ticks COUNTS SIGHTINGS, NOT ELAPSED TICKS, and the gap test is per-gap rather than cumulative. So a member sighted once every 20 ticks accumulates a qualifying stay whose start is far older than MIN_TICKS — each individual gap is within tolerance, so nothing splits the stay, while the sighting count crawls to the threshold over a much longer wall-clock span. Not a defect (the real decoration stream is per-tick, so this is the blackout case rather than the normal one), but TrackedRoom.onPresence's KDoc should say ticks are sightings, because 'ticks' reads as elapsed time and a future reader will assume it bounds the stay's length.

(2) THE GAP TOLERANCE IS CALIBRATED, NOT MEASURED. MIN_TICKS as the gap that may not split a stay is reasoned from PartyTracker.positions' documented 10-20 tick roster-skew window around a death, with ZERO MARGIN — 20 against a documented worst case of 20. If the real blackout ever runs one tick longer, a stay splits and the room anchors on the return instead of the arrival. Settled by the first real debug session, not by any command here.

(3) anchorOnClear's REAL-FLOOR FREQUENCY IS UNKNOWN. The fallback is bounded by construction (it can never invent a span longer than one second), so how often it fires is a question about data quality rather than correctness — but if it fires on most rooms, the anchor is mostly a fallback and the feature bought less than it looks like. The 'room_anchored' debug event and the cleared event's anchoredOnClear flag exist to answer exactly this; both need a real run, so this rides with ingame-001.

features.notes:
NOT a schema change and NOT paired with the receiver. Checked against its source rather than assumed, as CLAUDE.md requires before touching anything schema-shaped: (a) RUN_KEYS (ingest.py:137) and ROOM_KEYS (ingest.py:152) carry NO per-player points field at all — the breakdown never leaves the client, so weighting is invisible to the validator; (b) `unattributed` is validated as _real(x, 0, MAX_CLEARED) with MAX_CLEARED=200 (ingest.py:167,226), the same ceiling roomsCleared is bounded by, and no 400 is reachable from either the old or the new definition; (c) the values the field carries are unchanged, so nothing routes on `v` differently and RunReport.SCHEMA stays 5.

WHAT THE WEIGHTING IS: ContributionTracker.weightOf(room) = BASE_POINTS 1.0, plus a kind bonus (PUZZLE 1.5; TRAP, CHAMPION/MINIBOSS and BLOOD 1.0 each), plus 0.25 per secret the room database says the room holds, plus 0.5 per segment beyond the first. The split over the members in the room is unchanged — proportional to time, MIN_TICKS filter, raw-presence fallback — so two players in one room are still separated only by time. THREE DELIBERATE EXCLUSIONS, each of which is the obvious next edit and each of which would measure the wrong thing: RARE gets nothing, because a rare room is unusual to draw rather than harder to clear and what makes it worth entering is its secret count, already paid for; secrets come from the database and not from room.secretsFound, because award() fires on the clear checkmark while the room's secrets are usually still being collected, so the live counter would weight most rooms at whatever they were part-way through; and the floor is NOT a multiplier, though DungeonSession.floorNumber is right there and the README listed it as an input — it is constant across every room of a run, so it scales every player's total equally and separates nobody, and points are only ever compared within one run because they are not in the run report at all. Revisit only if points ever become something the server stores. An unnamed room (chunk never streamed, info null) keeps its kind from the map colour and pays no secret bonus: worth less than it should be, never nothing.

EXCLUSION COVERAGE, corrected in session 006 after the 12/14 evaluation, because an artifact said these were guarded when two of the three were not. RARITY: pinned, 'a rare room is not paid for being rare'. SECRETS FROM THE DATABASE: pinned as of 390399b, by 'the live secret counter is not what a room is worth' (both the additive and the substituting edit) and by 'the credit is the whole room even though the checkmark lands mid-collection', which pins the reason rather than a number — award() fires on the checkmark while the party is still collecting, so the live counter at that instant is a race and the same room would be worth different amounts depending only on when the last mob dropped. FLOOR: PINNED as of session 007, by 'a room is worth the same on every floor'. Sessions 005 and 006 recorded the opposite — that a floor guard was impossible here because DungeonSession.floor is 'private set' behind inDungeon(Minecraft), so a floor factor would read null under test and any such test would 'pass either way'. THAT WAS FALSE, and the second evaluator disproved it by construction: DungeonSession::class.java.getDeclaredField("floor") with isAccessible = true reaches the object's backing field, and floorNumber then reads the real digit. The test checks three floors (F1 vs F7 catches a factor drawn from floorNumber; F7 vs M7 catches one drawn from the floor STRING, which is how a master-mode bonus would be written and which floorNumber cannot see; Entrance is the null reading every other test runs under) and asserts BOTH the weight and the credited points, since a floor factor could be applied in weightOf or between it and the split in award. Critically it asserts that the reflective write took — assertEquals(1, DungeonSession.floorNumber) — BEFORE it asserts the invariant, which is the whole difference between a guard and a guard in name only; neutering setFloor makes the case fail with 'the floor was not actually set'. THE COST, recorded rather than hidden: this is the only reflection in the suite, so a rename of DungeonSession.floor breaks the test at runtime rather than at compile time. Accepted deliberately over the alternative the earlier sessions proposed — a production seam on DungeonSession — because that is a shape src/main does not otherwise need, added purely for a test, and it is a bigger change than the exclusion is worth. WHAT THIS COST TO MISS: under a live floor multiplier all 119 tests at 72e0825 passed. The exclusion was guarded by nothing, while three artifacts said it was unguardable.

THE LOAD-BEARING HALF, and the reason this feature is not just a formula. `unattributed` was `roomsCleared - pointsByPlayer().values.sum()`. That expression was only ever correct because a room was worth exactly 1.0 point, which made a COUNT and a SCORE numerically interchangeable. Weighted, the score routinely exceeds the room count, the subtraction goes negative, and settle()'s clamp reports 0.0 on every run forever — no exception, no 400, no log line, a field that stops saying anything while looking perfect. Same failure shape this project has spent two sessions removing elsewhere. So the count is now COUNTED, in award(), at the one place the decision is made (ContributionTracker.unattributedRooms), and it stays in ROOMS: a heavy room nobody was in is one unattributed room, not five points of one. That is not a preference — the receiver reads this field RELATIVE to roomsCleared and it is its only diagnostic for a broken decoration->player mapping (its agent/AGENT-PROMPT.md line 62), and a ratio of a score to a count means nothing at either end. WHY NO SCHEMA BUMP IS OWED: under flat weighting every award credited either the full point or nothing, so the old subtraction already produced exactly this count (give or take the float residue residue-001 removed). Same meaning, same numbers, now by construction instead of by coincidence — which is the opposite of clear-001, where the key stayed and the meaning moved.

NEW SEAM: ContributionTracker.onCleared(room) is internal and does roomsCleared++ then award(room). tick() calls it. This closes the gap session 002 recorded — 'unattributed()'s composition has no test, because roomsCleared and credited are private and only a real run fills them' — since onCleared needs a cleared room and nothing else, while tick() still needs a Minecraft and a MapItemSavedData. DebugLog.event was measured to be safe under the test runtime (it resolves Config and FabricLoader without throwing), which is what makes driving award() from a test possible at all.

NOT SHIPPED: no version bump, no dist/ refresh, so this reaches no install until the next release, which is the user's decision. rooms.json was read and never written.

features.title: Weight a room by how long it actually takes, not by what kind it is
features.user_visible_behavior: A room is worth what it costs the party: 0.75 for clearing it, plus 0.25 per secret, plus or minus however far its measured clear time sits from the average room. A slow room scores higher than a fast one without anybody deciding that a puzzle is worth 1.5.
verification_manual: Compare two rooms of the same kind with very different measured averages and confirm the slower one scores higher.
Confirm a room with no measured average scores exactly the 0.75 base plus its secrets, and is not silently treated as fast.
Play a floor and confirm the point spread still separates party members the way the flat count could not.
features.blocked_reason: BLOCKED ON DATA, NOT ON CODE. The model needs per-room measured clear times and they barely exist yet: /srv/sighte/roomstats.json carries 83 rooms and only 9 have any clear sample at all, every one of them n=1. Weighting off a single observation is worse than the constants it replaces. Worse, those 9 samples were folded under the OLD first-sighting anchor, which is an upper bound a walk-through inflates - the stay-anchored `clearStay` block is empty (n=0) for all 83 rooms and stays that way until a schema 5 build is RELEASED, because every installed build still sends schema 4. So the chain is: release -> runs accumulate -> averages become real -> this feature becomes implementable. Nothing in the code blocks it.
features.notes:
THE USER'S DESIGN, 2026-08-14, and it replaces clearpoints-001's formula rather than extending it: '1 Secret EGAL welcher Raum = +0.25, alle anderen Raeume haben einen Base Score von 0.75, und abhaengig davon wie schnell der durchschnittliche Spieler diesen Raum cleart (KEINE SECRETS) geht dieser Wert hoch oder auch runter.'

WHAT IT DELETES: PUZZLE_BONUS, TRAP_BONUS, MINIBOSS_BONUS, BLOOD_BONUS and SEGMENT_POINTS - five hand-picked constants. They become emergent instead of declared: a puzzle scores high because puzzles measure slow, a four-segment room scores high because crossing it takes time. That is the whole point and it is a better one than the constants, because a constant is an opinion and an average is a measurement. BASE_POINTS goes 1.0 -> 0.75. SECRET_POINTS stays 0.25 and stays keyed on the room database's secret count rather than secretsFound, for the reason clearpoints-001 already has a test on: award() fires on the checkmark while secrets are still being collected.

WHICH NUMBER IS 'the average player clearing it, no secrets': roomstats.json's `clearStay` block, not `clear` and not `afterClear`. clearStay is the minimum-stay anchor clear-001 ships; afterClear is explicitly the post-checkmark secret hunt and is what 'KEINE SECRETS' excludes.

THE MECHANISM IS NOT DECIDED AND IT IS THE HARD PART. The mod is client-side; the averages live on the receiver. Three options: (a) ship a snapshot of roomstats.json inside the jar, regenerated at release time; (b) fetch it from the receiver at startup; (c) derive it from the player's own history.jsonl. RECOMMENDATION (a), for a reason that decides it rather than a preference: points are compared BETWEEN party members, so two clients that fetched at different times would score the same room differently and the standings would disagree about a run both of them watched. A snapshot pinned to the jar makes the weights reproducible per version, needs no network, adds no failure mode, and is regenerated by the same release step that already exists. (c) answers a different question - it weights by how fast YOU are, not the average player.

THE CURVE IS ALSO UNDECIDED. 'goes up or down' needs a shape: a ratio against the median room, clamped at both ends so one 36-second outlier cannot make a room worth ten. Pick it from the real distribution once there is one - choosing it now would be exactly the guesswork this feature removes.

Judging every room separately per floor was called too much for a mod this size: 'es waere einfach zu viel fuer jeden floor jeden raum einzeln zu bewerten also bleiben die Raeume global erstmal'. features.notes:
THE BLEND IS DELIBERATE. A room that appears on more than one floor keeps ONE record and ONE average across all of them, and a room genuinely harder on F7 than on F5 therefore reports a number that describes neither exactly. That is accepted. The receiver already behaves the same way on purpose: roomstats.py folds per room name and carries `floors` only as a list beside the averages, so keeping this deferred costs nothing on either side and needs no paired feature.

README 'Not implemented yet': /sa collapses floors into one record per room and kind. The data is already there — the history lines carry floor — so this is a fold and a filter, not a capture change. Watch RoomHistory.kt:59: the whole history is in memory.

features.notes:
README 'Known limits': the build compiles and the grid, timing and tab-parsing logic are unit tested, but calibration, decoration mapping, checkmark reading and core hashing have never run against real Hypixel data. The /sa screen is one step further down — its API use is pinned by the compiler and its record fold is unit tested, but no pixel of it has ever been on screen. Note also that the room database is version-coupled: core hashes are built from Block.toString() in a fixed order, so RoomDatabase.coreAt must be re-verified whenever Hypixel changes a room or Mojang changes that representation.

WHAT TO READ OUT OF THE FIRST REAL SESSION FILE, beyond the list above — three open review findings are waiting on exactly this data and are recorded in full on the features they belong to (session 006): clear-001's gap tolerance, calibrated against PartyTracker's documented 10-20 tick blackout with zero margin and never measured; anchorOnClear's real-floor frequency, answerable from the 'room_anchored' events and the cleared event's anchoredOnClear flag; and clearpoints-001's weight constants, which are judgement rather than measurement and which no unit test can validate — that 1.5 for a puzzle and 0.25 a secret separate players in a way a player would agree with needs a run.

features.title: run_end carries the field the receiver's analysis agent is told to read
features.user_visible_behavior: An analyst opening a debug session can read `unattributed` against `roomsCleared` in one event, the way the receiver's own runbook says to.
verification_manual: Capture a debug session from a real run.
Find the run_end line and verify it carries both roomsCleared and unattributed.
features.notes: FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING clearpoints-001, recorded rather than fixed inline per CLAUDE.md. The receiver's agent/AGENT-PROMPT.md line 62 tells its analysis agent to look for '`unattributed` large relative to `roomsCleared` in `run_end`' — that gap is the documented diagnostic for a broken decoration->player mapping. The mod's run_end event (SighteAddons.kt:149) writes floor, roomsCleared, points, unnamed and newRecords, and NOT unattributed. So the receiver's runbook names a field that has never been in the log, and an analyst following it finds a hole rather than a signal. This is a one-field addition to a debug event: not a schema change, not paired (DebugLog is the mod's own JSONL and the receiver does not validate it), and no version bump. Worth doing deliberately anyway, because the alternative reading is that AGENT-PROMPT.md meant the per-room `unattributed` EVENT that award() emits, in which case the fix is on the receiver's side of the wire and is a different delegation — decide which before writing the line. Note also that the per-room `unattributed` event fires whenever the MIN_TICKS split was empty, including when the raw-presence fallback then credited somebody, so counting those events is NOT the same number as the run's unattributed rooms; whoever picks this up should say which of the two the analyst wants.
